name: Powers of two and byte order
brief: `next_pow2(x)` is the smallest power of two that is at least `x`. It is 1 for 0 or 1, and `x` is at most 2^30. `is_pow2(x)` is true for 1, 2, 4, 8 and so on, and false for 0. `popcount(x)` is the number of 1 bits. `bswap32(x)` reverses the four bytes of `x`.
constraints: Use unsigned arithmetic, so shifts never overflow a signed value.
Do not use compiler built-ins: write the loops and masks yourself.
hint: A power of two has one bit set, so `x & (x - 1)` is 0. For `popcount`, `x &= x - 1` clears the lowest set bit.
how: Fifteen hidden tests cover each function: zero, powers of two, 2^30, all bits set, and byte swaps. Results above 2,147,483,647 are cast to `long long` in the test so they compare exactly.
notes: `(x >> 8) & 0xFF00` moves byte 2 down; `(x << 8) & 0xFF0000` moves byte 1 up.
